# RFC: Visual-First Build Workflow, Screenshot Translation & Skill Architecture Safeguards ## 1. Executive Summary & Purpose This RFC documents the analysis of Timothy Ricks' video and the **Lumos for Astro** framework, evaluating their applicability to the `emdash-site-starter` workflow: * **Reference Video:** [Timothy Ricks: "Figma to Astro" (YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z2-WESZxSgM) * **Framework Reference:** [Lumos Framework Documentation](https://lumosframework.com/docs/) In our typical workflow, we frequently build or migrate Astro sites from **existing WordPress sites, visual references, or flat screenshots** rather than structured Figma tokens. This RFC addresses two core objectives: 1. **Framework & Workflow Evaluation:** Evaluate whether to adopt Lumos for Astro versus our current stack (Astro + Tailwind CSS v4 `@theme` + EmDash CMS), and extract actionable design, motion, and prompt engineering techniques. 2. **Skill Architecture & Upstream Protection:** Establish an upgrade-safe architecture to incorporate these workflow improvements without modifying third-party upstream skills like `impeccable` (which would be clobbered by skill updates or sync scripts). --- ## 2. Analysis of the Reference Workflow (Timothy Ricks: "Figma to Astro") ### Context * **Source:** [Watch on YouTube (z2-WESZxSgM)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z2-WESZxSgM) * **Scenario:** Rebuilding a visual design in Astro where the Figma mockup contained **no design system, no defined spacing tokens, no color variables, and no component structure**. * **AI Toolchain:** ChatGPT / Codex / Astra + **Stacki** (visual builder/inspector for Astro) + **Lumos for Astro** (`lumosframework.com`). * **Key Characteristic:** Because API/plugin authentication was initially missing, the agent was effectively operating from **flat visual evidence / screenshots**. ### Common Failure Modes Observed During AI Generation When an LLM agent was given visual screenshots without rigid constraints, it repeatedly reverted to several destructive habits: 1. **Hardcoded Palette Values:** Referencing raw palette colors (e.g. `light-100` or raw hex) directly on element styles rather than semantic theme tokens (`--color-text`, `--color-surface`, `--color-action`), completely breaking light/dark mode toggling. 2. **Layout Line Breaking with `
`:** Inserting hardcoded `
` tags into headings to mimic visual mockup wrapping rather than using container `max-width`, responsive measure (`ch`), or CSS `text-wrap: balance / pretty`. 3. **Naked Structural Elements:** Leaving buttons, links, and `
` tags floating orphan outside layout `
` and `` boundaries. 4. **Grid Track Blowout:** Defining grid column tracks with plain `1fr` rather than `minmax(0, 1fr)`, leading to intrinsic content overflow and page blowout. 5. **Rasterization of Vector Assets:** Exporting SVG icons as raster `` PNGs instead of inline SVGs or `` components, breaking hover effects and `currentColor` inheritance. 6. **"AI Slop" on Unseen Pages:** When instructed to extrapolate new pages without visual mockups, the AI generated walls of verbose marketing text, distorted button geometries, and inconsistent layouts. ### Successful Steering Patterns Observed * **Metric Preflight:** Inspecting font line-heights and bounding box trim (*trim-top*) early to ensure text boxes hug typography without "ghost margins." * **Context / Stream Segregation:** Maintaining separate conversational threads for distinct concerns: * `Macro Layout & Structure` * `Theme & Semantic Tokens` * `Animations & Scroll Mechanics` (Lenis, sticky pinned sections, parallax) * `Micro-Interactions & WebGL` * **"Fix Globally, Not Locally" Directives:** When catching an anti-pattern (e.g. bad icon tag or hardcoded color), instructing the agent: *"You made this mistake here; audit and fix it everywhere across the project."* * **External Interaction Recipe Porting:** Taking production-grade interaction snippets from curated libraries (e.g. Osmo, CodePen), stripping vendor boilerplate, and prompting the agent to rebuild them strictly in native CSS bound to project tokens. * **Instant Visual Verification:** Using on-screen column grid overlays toggled by a hotkey (`G`) to verify alignment against design columns in real time. --- ## 3. Framework Evaluation: Why We Reject Lumos for Astro While Lumos provides a solid educational system for developers transitioning from Webflow's *Client-First* system to Astro, **we recommend against replacing our current setup with Lumos.** | Evaluation Vector | Our Current Setup (`emdash-site-starter`) | Lumos for Astro (`lumosframework.com`) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **CMS Alignment** | **Native EmDash integration** via live collection field edit proxies (`editProxy`), Portable Text (`.flow` / `RichText.astro`), and SQLite/Cloudflare D1 schemas. | Static/marketing-oriented. Has no concept of EmDash proxies, translation groups, or CMS content schemas. | | **Styling Engine** | **Tailwind CSS v4 (`@theme`)** + modern CSS primitives. Zero config, ultra-fast compilation, fluid interpolation scales. | Custom CSS `@layer` system with Webflow Client-First class conventions (`.u-section`, `.u-text-style-h1`). | | **DOM Abstraction** | **Lightweight structural primitives** (`Section`, `Container`, `Grid`). Elements remain semantic native HTML. | **Heavy wrapper components** (``, ``, ``, ``) that add unnecessary abstraction over native HTML. | | **Visual Editing** | Code-first + EmDash editorial canvas + `` scalar calibration. | Tightly coupled with **Stacki** visual builder. | **Verdict:** Adopting Lumos would introduce redundant abstraction layers that interfere with EmDash field-proxy bindings and replace Tailwind v4 with a verbose BEM utility system. We should borrow the **methodologies**, not the framework. --- ## 4. Key Methodologies to Incorporate into Our Workflow ### A. Visual Preflight Sequence (Before Coding Pages) When working from screenshots or an existing WordPress site: 1. **Font & Metric Preflight:** Extract font families, load local assets into `src/assets/fonts/`, and account for font metric bounding-box trim. 2. **Semantic Theme Mapping:** Map visual colors immediately to semantic roles (`page`, `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `action`, `border`), even if the source reference is single-mode. 3. **Macro Grid Detection:** Count the underlying column grid (e.g. 10 vs 12 columns) and define container bounds. ### B. The External Interaction Recipe Porting Protocol When sleek interactions (button hover physics, sticky pinned masks, parallax) are needed from references: * Source clean CSS/HTML from reference libraries (Osmo, CodePen). * Use the prompt protocol: *"Ignore the external class names and markup structure in this snippet. Re-implement this interaction pattern using pure CSS, binding all colors and measurements directly to our existing `@theme` tokens and Astro layout primitives."* * *(Tracked in Issue #2 for legacy site backporting, and Issue #7 for visual regression testing).* ### C. Anti-Slop Extrapolation Guardrails When generating secondary pages that lack direct screenshots: * Impose strict copy budgets (e.g. maximum word counts for headings and paragraphs). * Mandate the reuse and recomposition of established homepage section archetypes rather than inventing new component geometries. ### D. Dedicated Verification Surfaces (Cross-Referenced Issues) * **Living Component Styleguide (Issue #5):** Implement `src/pages/_styleguide.astro` so the agent has a single unified surface to verify all typography, buttons, cards, and theme variations. * **In-Browser Dev HUD (Issue #6):** Implement hotkeys in `` for Column Grid Guide (`G`), Screenshot Diff Overlay (`O`), and EmDash Proxy Inspector (`P`). * **Visual Regression Suite (Issue #7):** Add automated headless screenshot diffing in CI to catch visual drift. --- ## 5. Architectural Problem: Protecting Upstream Skills ### The Dilemma * `.agents/skills/impeccable/` is a pinned third-party skill (v4.3.1). * The starter maintains synchronization via `scripts/sync-site-skills.mjs` and upstream repository tracking. * **If we edit `impeccable/` directly**, our modifications will be lost during syncs or updates. * Moreover, `impeccable` is scoped for **design critique and polish**, not initial page construction from visual mockups. ### Architectural Options ``` [Always-On System Rules] (.agent/rules/ & workspace AGENTS.md) │ ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ [astro-site-design] [impeccable] (Vermeulen-maintained skill for (Untouched 3rd-party visual evidence implementation) critique & polish skill) ``` #### Option 1: The Rule Bridge Pattern (Recommended) 1. **Leave `impeccable/` 100% untouched.** 2. **Add the detailed reference to `astro-site-design`:** Create `.agents/skills/astro-site-design/references/visual-mockup-workflow.md` documenting the preflight order, recipe porting protocol, grid defense, and anti-slop copy budgets. 3. **Add an always-on rule in `.agent/rules/visual-craft.md`:** An always-on rule ensures that whether the agent is in discovery, implementing via `astro-site-design`, or running a polish pass via `impeccable`, the visual standards (theme token immunity, `minmax(0, 1fr)` grids, copy budgets) are active in the system prompt. #### Option 2: Standalone Skill (`visual-reference-craft`) 1. Create a dedicated skill in `.agents/skills/visual-reference-craft/SKILL.md`. 2. Add a rule in `.agent/rules/` instructing agents to load this skill whenever working from visual references or external CSS recipes. * *Trade-off:* Clean separation, but creates another skill to maintain when `astro-site-design` already owns visual evidence implementation. --- ## 6. Questions for Second Agent Review / Feedback Requested 1. **Option 1 vs. Option 2:** Does the **Rule Bridge Pattern (Option 1)** provide sufficient guidance across agent harnesses, or is a dedicated standalone skill (Option 2) preferable for multi-agent workflows? 2. **Rule Enforcement:** Are the proposed guardrails (`minmax(0, 1fr)`, no layout `
` tags, strict semantic token routing, copy budgets) complete, or are there additional failure modes common to visual-to-code LLM pipelines that should be codified? 3. **Tooling Synergy:** How should the newly defined Living Styleguide (Issue #5) and TweaksBar HUD (Issue #6) be surfaced to coding agents during visual passes?
title: RFC: Visual-First Build Workflow, Screenshot Translation & Skill Architecture Safeguards
